The above-captioned four appeals and two revision petitions are being taken up together for
discussion and adjudication as these have arisen out of the single Award passed by learned Motor
Accident Claims Tribunal, Rewari (for short 'the Tribunal') on 09.11.2005, whereby six claim
petitions, pertaining to the same motor vehicular accident, have been decided and thus, common
questions of law and facts are involved therein.

sentences.text:
Shorn and short of unnecessary details, the facts, culminating in the filing of the present appeals and the revision petitions, are that on the fateful day, i.e 12.06.2000, Rajender, Rajesh, Narender,
Yad Ram, Sachin, Dharmender and some other persons, were returning to Village Nangal Sarohi from Village Jatuwas in the Four-Wheeler bearing Registration No. HR-38-0665 (for short 'the offending vehicle') after attending the marriage ceremony of one Vikas and the dowry-items were also being transported in this vehicle which was being driven by the respondent-driver in a rash and negligent manner.

When they reached near Naya Gaon turn, the said vehicle turned turtle and resultantly, all the afore-named persons sustained injuries in this accident and the same,
unfortunately, proved fatal for said Rajender, Rajesh and Narender.
3. Respondents No.1 & 2 (in FAO No.1166 of 2006) namely Suraj Bhan and Smt. Santra,
respondents No.1 & 2 (in FAO No.1167 of 2006) named Ram Parshad and Smt. Saraswati, the respective parents of deceased Rajesh and Narender and respondents No.1 to 7 (in FAO No.1169 of 2006), i.e Smt. Roopwati etc, being the wife, five children and mother of deceased Rajender, filed separate petitions for claiming compensation on account of their death and injured-Yad Ram,
Sachin and Dharmender also moved the petitions for seeking compensation for the injuries suffered by them, in the above-said accident.
4. All the respondents, i.e the driver, owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle, filed their separate written statements contesting the claims, as set-forth by the claimants in their respective petitions, on various 3 of 8 Neutral Citation No:= FAO No.1166 of 2006 and other connected cases -4- grounds.
Then, the Tribunal put the parties to the trial by framing the issues in the first set of four consolidated petitions and in the second set of two petitions as well.

After appreciating and evaluating the evidence as led by the parties on the record and hearing their learned counsels, the Tribunal passed the impugned Award, granting the compensation to the claimants, while observing that they (claimants) would be entitled to recover the same from the respondents, jointly and (O&M) Oriental Ins. 3 severally and the Insurance Company, would be liable to indemnify the insured-owner.

entities.text: Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd vs Suraj Bhan & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have heard learned respective counsels for the appellant- petitioner-Insurance Company as well as for the respondents, i.e the claimants, the owner and driver of the offending vehicle, in these appeals and revision petitions and have also gone through the record carefully.

6. At the very outset, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that he intends to raise the contentions only qua the observations made by the Tribunal in the impugned Award, regarding the liability of the Insurance Company to pay the amount of compensation, meaning thereby that the sole controversy that, now, survives in the instant cases for the adjudication by this Court, is confined to the above-discussed extent only.

7. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company contends that the afore-named deceased and injured persons were travelling in the offending vehicle as the unauthorised/gratuitous passengers as they were neither the owners nor the authorised representatives of the owner of the goods, i.e the dowry articles, which were being transported in the said vehicle at the time of the above-referred accident and the Insurance Policy, issued in respect of 4 of 8 Neutral Citation No:= FAO No.1166 of 2006 and other connected cases -5- this vehicle, did not cover the risk of such passengers and therefore, the Insurance Company could not have been saddled with the liability to pay the amount of compensation, as awarded by the Tribunal.
8.

However, learned counsels for the respondents-claimants, the driver and the owner of the offending vehicle, argue that the afore-named deceased as well as the injured persons were the members of the marriage party and after attending the marriage, they were returning to their native village along-with the dowry articles, as being carried in the offending vehicle and thus, they were the authorised representatives of the owner of these goods and hence, the risk qua their death or bodily injury was very well covered under the Insurance Policy issued by the Insurance Company for the said vehicle and it being so, the Insurance Company cannot be allowed to escape its liability to pay the award amount.
9.

It goes undisputed between the parties that the above-named deceased as well as the injured persons had gone to Village Jatuwas to attend the marriage of Vikas and that at the time of the afore-said accident, they were returning to their village in the offending vehicle, which was carrying the dowry items.

Annexure R2 (available in the record of Claim Petition No.286 of 2000) is the Certificate-cum-Policy Schedule issued in respect of the said vehicle wherein it is shown to have been insured as the 'Goods Carrying Commercial Vehicle Policy 'A' Act only' and this fact makes it crystal clear that this vehicle was a 'Goods Carrying Vehicle'.

Section 147(1)(b)(i) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 had been amended in the year 1994, whereby the words "including owner of the goods or his 5 of 8 Neutral Citation No:= FAO No.1166 of 2006 and other connected cases -6- authorised representative" were added therein.

In para No.39 of the impugned Award, the Tribunal has held that the said passengers were travelling in the offending vehicle as the authorised representatives of the owner of the goods, i.e the dowry items.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, it is worth-while to point it out here that while appearing as PW7, claimant-injured Yad Ram (examined in the above-said Claim Petition) has categorically deposed during his cross-examination that the goods, loaded in the offending vehicle, did not belong to them and rather, these were the dowry articles and none of the owners of the same was travelling along-with them.

Further, PW-8 Sachin, another claimant- injured (examined in the same Claim Petition) has also specifically stated during his cross-examination that none had asked him to sit/travel in the said vehicle.

To add to it, a perusal of Exhibit PW4/1, the copy of FIR No.120 dated 13.06.2000,
registered at Police Station Sadar Rewari, under Sections 279, 337, 338 and 304-A IPC, regarding the afore-said accident (annexed in the record of the same petition), reveals that informant Sunil Kumar had stated before the police that the above-named deceased and the injured persons and some other persons had gone to Village Jatuwas in the offending vehicle, to attend the marriage of Vikas and were returning from there in the same vehicle and he has no-where mentioned in his statement, as detailed in the said FIR, that they had been asked by the owner of the goods, as being transported in the said vehicle, to accompany the same as his/her representatives.

In these circumstances, the afore-said passengers cannot be construed to be the owners or the authorised representatives of 6 of 8 Neutral Citation No:= FAO No.1166 of 2006 and other connected cases -7- the owner(s) of the goods loaded in the offending vehicle.
Consequently, the above-discussed findings as returned by the Tribunal on this point, being erroneous, are hereby reversed accordingly.

11. It has categorically been observed by the three Judges' Bench of Hon'ble the Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Baljit Kaur & Others (2004) AIR (SC) 1340 that "the liability of the owner of the vehicle to insure it compulsorily, thus, by the reason of 1994 Amendment in Section 147 of the Act of 1988, included only the owner of the goods or his authorised representatives carried in the vehicle besides the third party and that the intention of the Parliament, therefore,

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Baljit Kaur & Others (2004) AIR (SC) 1340
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: could not have been that the words 'any person' occurring in Section 147 would cover all persons who were travelling in a goods carriage in any capacity whatsoever".

These observations are fully applicable to the instant cases and in view of the same, the Insurance Company cannot be fastened with the liability to indemnify the insured qua the amount of compensation as awarded by the Tribunal in all the six claim petitions and rather, the respondents-driver and owner of the offending vehicle, would be jointly as well as severally liable to pay the same.

12. As a sequel to the fore-going discussion, all the four appeals and both the revision petitions in hand, are hereby allowed to the effect that the Insurance Company stands exonerated/absolved from the liability to pay the amount of compensation to the respondents-claimants and rather, the respondents-driver and owner of the offending vehicle, shall be liable to pay the same.

It is further clarified that in case, the Insurance Company has 7 of 8 Neutral Citation No:= FAO No.1166 of 2006 and other connected cases -8- already satisfied the claim of the respondents-claimants, then it shall have the right to recover the award amount, as paid by it to them (claimants), from the respondents-owner and the driver of the offending vehicle, by resorting to the relevant procedure, as prescribed for this purpose.
